Chapter 8: The Ultimate Purpose — God’s Glory and Our Joy
Have you ever found yourself wondering, late at night or during some quiet moment, what’s it all really for? It’s a question that’s always there, quietly tugging at the edges of our daily routines. We all search for meaning—no matter our age, our background, or what we’re going through. Some people chase after success, others just want to feel comfortable, and a lot of us are just trying to make it through the day. Underneath it all, though, there’s this deep longing for something more—a sense that life must be about more than just getting by.
Now, you might’ve heard that God’s glory is supposed to be the ultimate purpose of life. But honestly, that idea can feel a little overwhelming, right? It brings up questions like, "Am I really significant?" or, "Does my happiness even matter?" But as we walk this path, something amazing starts to happen: we realize that God’s glory and our own joy aren’t competing—they’re actually connected. They’re like two sides of the same coin.
Let me share a story. Picture someone who’s spent years climbing the ladder—achieving, collecting awards, building a reputation. But after all that striving, there’s still this emptiness, a restlessness that just won’t go away. Then, in a rare moment of stillness, it finally hits them: real, lasting joy isn’t found in promoting ourselves. It comes from being swept up into something far bigger. When we start living for God’s glory, we discover a fulfillment that all our accomplishments could never provide.
The truth is, most of us settle for smaller purposes—like career success, a good reputation, or just a comfortable life—without ever stopping to ask if there’s something more. But when our focus shifts from ourselves to God’s glory, everything else seems to find its right place. Instead of frantically searching for meaning, life becomes a journey of discovery. The more we delight in God, the more our lives start to shine with His greatness.
And here’s where things really come into focus. Seeing life this way helps us make sense of all the highs and lows. Whether we’re winning or losing, celebrating or grieving, gaining or letting go—it’s all woven into a much bigger story. Our ultimate purpose isn’t just to avoid pain or chase after pleasure. It’s to find deep, unshakable joy in God, no matter what’s happening around us. That kind of joy becomes our anchor—holding us steady in every season of life.
